Main.sentence: The Islamic Resistance Movement , abbreviated Hamas [a] (an acronym from the ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ : حركة المقاومة الإسلامية , romanized: Ḥarakat al-Muqāwamah al-ʾIslāmiyyah ),  [b] is a ___E:Sunni U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunni_Islam)___ ___E:Islamist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamism)___ ___E:Palestinian nationalist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_nationalist)___  political organisation with a military wing, the ___E:al-Qassam Brigades U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qassam_Brigades)___ .

It has ___E:governed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip_under_Hamas)___ the ___E:Israeli-occupied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ since 2007.

The Hamas movement was founded by Palestinian Islamic scholar ___E:Ahmed Yassin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Yassin)___ in 1987, after the outbreak of the ___E:First Intifada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Intifada)___ against the Israeli occupation.

It emerged from his 1973 ___E:Mujama al-Islamiya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mujama_al-Islamiya)___ Islamic charity affiliated with the ___E:Muslim Brotherhood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood)___ .

Initially, Hamas was discreetly supported by ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ , as a counter-balance to the secular Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) to prevent the creation of an independent Palestinian state.

In the 2006 ___E:Palestinian legislative election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Palestinian_legislative_election)___ , Hamas secured a majority in the ___E:Palestinian Legislative Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Legislative_Council)___ by campaigning on promises of a corruption-free government and advocating for resistance as a means to liberate Palestine from Israeli occupation.

In the 2007 ___E:Battle of Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gaza_(2007))___ , Hamas seized control of the Gaza Strip from rival Palestinian faction ___E:Fatah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah)___ ,   and has since governed the territory separately from the ___E:Palestinian National Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority)___ .

After Hamas's takeover, Israel significantly intensified existing movement restrictions and imposed a complete ___E:blockade of the Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip)___ .

Egypt also began its blockade of Gaza at this time. This was followed by multiple wars with Israel, including those ___E:in 2008–09 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_War_(2008%E2%80%932009))___ , ___E:2012 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Gaza_War)___ , ___E:2014 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Gaza_War)___ , ___E:2021 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Israel%E2%80%93Palestine_crisis)___ , and ___E:an ongoing one since 2023 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ , which began with the ___E:October 7 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks)___ .

Hamas has promoted Palestinian nationalism in an ___E:Islamic context U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_nationalism)___  and initially sought a state in all of former ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ .

It began acquiescing to 1967 borders in the agreements it signed with Fatah in ___E:2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Cairo_Declaration)___ , ___E:2006 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Prisoners%27_Document)___ and ___E:2007 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah%E2%80%93Hamas_Mecca_Agreement)___ .

In 2017, Hamas released a ___E:new charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Document_of_General_Principles_and_Policies)___  that supported a Palestinian state within the 1967 borders without recognizing Israel.

Hamas's repeated offers of a ___E:truce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudna)___ (for a period of 10–100 years  : 221–246 ) based on the 1967 borders are seen by many as consistent with a ___E:two-state solution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-state_solution)___ ,   while others state that Hamas retains the long-term objective of establishing one state in former Mandatory Palestine.  : 837, 839 While the ___E:1988 Hamas charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Hamas_charter)___ was widely described as ___E:antisemitic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism)___ ,  Hamas's 2017 charter  removed the antisemitic language and declared ___E:Zionists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionism)___ , not Jews, the targets of their struggle.
It has been debated whether the charter has reflected an actual change in policy.

In terms of foreign policy, Hamas has historically sought out relations with Egypt,  Iran,  Qatar,  Saudi Arabia,  Syria  and Turkey;  some of its relations have been impacted by the ___E:Arab Spring U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Spring)___ .

Hamas and Israel have engaged in the protracted ___E:Gaza–Israel conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza%E2%80%93Israel_conflict)___ , as part of the broader ___E:Israeli–Palestinian conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli%E2%80%93Palestinian_conflict)___ .

Hamas has attacked Israeli civilians, including through ___E:suicide bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_suicide_attacks)___ as well as ___E:launching rockets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_rocket_attacks_on_Israel)___ at Israeli cities.

Australia, Canada, Ecuador, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, Paraguay, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the European Union have designated Hamas as a ___E:terrorist organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_designated_terrorist_groups)___ .
In 2018 and 2023, motions at the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations)___ to condemn Hamas failed to meet the two-thirds threshold. [c]

Hamas is an ___E:acronym U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acronym)___ of the ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ phrase حركة المقاومة الإسلامية or Ḥarakah al-Muqāwamah al-ʾIslāmiyyah , meaning "Islamic Resistance Movement".

This acronym, HMS, was ___E:glossed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gloss_(annotation))___ in the ___E:1988 Hamas Covenant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Hamas_charter)___  by the Arabic word ḥamās ( حماس ) which itself means "zeal", "strength", or "bravery".

Hamas was established in 1987, and allegedly has its origins in ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ 's ___E:Muslim Brotherhood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Brotherhood)___ movement,     which had been active in the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ since the 1950s and gained influence through a network of mosques and various charitable and social organizations.

Unlike other Palestinian factions, after the ___E:Israeli occupation of Gaza in 1967 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ , the Brotherhood in Gaza refused to join the resistance boycott against Israel.

In the 1980s, it emerged as a powerful political factor, challenging the influence of the ___E:PLO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLO)___ , whose ___E:Fatah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah)___ faction it had played a core role in creating.
In December 1987, the Brotherhood adopted a more nationalist and activist line under the name of Hamas.
Hamas was initially discreetly supported by Israel as a counter-balance to the secular ___E:PLO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLO)___ .
During the 1990s and early 2000s, the organization conducted numerous suicide bombings and other attacks against Israel.

In the Palestinian legislative election of January 2006, Hamas gained a large majority of seats in the ___E:Palestinian Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Parliament)___ , defeating the ruling ___E:Fatah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah)___ party.
After the elections, conflicts arose between Hamas and Fatah, which they were unable to resolve.

In June 2007, Hamas defeated Fatah in a ___E:series of violent clashes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatah-Hamas_conflict#Conflict)___ , and since that time Hamas has governed the ___E:Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ portion of the ___E:Palestinian territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_territories)___ , while at the same time they were ousted from government positions in the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ .   ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ and ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ then imposed an ___E:economic blockade on Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_blockade_on_Gaza)___ and largely sealed their borders with the territory.

After acquiring control of Gaza, Hamas-affiliated and other militias launched rocket attacks upon Israel, which Hamas ceased in June 2008 following an ___E:Egyptian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ -brokered ceasefire.
The ceasefire broke down late in 2008, with each side accusing the other of responsibility.

In late December 2008, ___E:Israel attacked Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%932009_Israel%E2%80%93Gaza_conflict)___ ,  withdrawing its forces in mid-January 2009.  Since 2009, Hamas has faced multiple military confrontations with Israel, notably the 2012 and 2014 Gaza Wars, leading to substantial casualties.
Hamas has maintained control over Gaza, often clashing with the Palestinian Authority led by Fatah.
Efforts at reconciliation between Hamas and Fatah have seen limited success.
Hamas continued to face international isolation and blockades, while engaging in sporadic rocket attacks and tunnel construction activities against Israel.
On 7 October 2023, Hamas and other Palestinian militants ___E:attacked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks)___ Israel killing nearly 1,200 Israelis, about two thirds of them civilians.

Approximately 250 Israeli civilians and soldiers were ___E:taken hostage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war_hostage_crisis)___ and brought to the Gaza Strip,  with the aim of securing the release of ___E:Palestinian prisoners in Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_prisoners_in_Israel)___ (as part of a prisoner swap).

Hamas said its attack was in response to Israel's ___E:continued occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ , ___E:blockade of Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip)___ , and ___E:settlements expansion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law_and_Israeli_settlements)___ , as well as alleged ___E:threats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Aqsa_is_in_danger)___ to the ___E:Al-Aqsa Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Aqsa_Mosque)___ and the plight of Palestinians.

There are also reports of ___E:sexual violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_and_gender-based_violence_in_the_7_October_attack_on_Israel)___ by Hamas militants, allegations that Hamas has denied.

Israel responded by ___E:invading the Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_invasion_of_the_Gaza_Strip_(2023%E2%80%93present))___ , killing over 70,000 Palestinians, 59.1% of them women, children and the elderly according to a peer-reviewed study in The Lancet .

On 31 July 2024, ___E:Ismail Haniyeh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismail_Haniyeh)___ was ___E:assassinated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Ismail_Haniyeh)___ in ___E:Tehran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran)___ , after attending the inauguration ceremony of Iranian president ___E:Masoud Pezeshkian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoud_Pezeshkian)___ .
In August 2024, ___E:Yahya Sinwar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahya_Sinwar)___ , the leader of Hamas in Gaza, was elected chairman of the group, replacing Haniyeh.

Per Hamas officials, he was elected due to his considerable popularity in the ___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world)___ and ___E:Islamic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_world)___ worlds following the ___E:7 October attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_October_attacks)___ and his strong connections with Iran and the " ___E:Axis of Resistance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_of_Resistance)___ ," an informal Iranian-led political and military coalition.
On 16 October 2024, IDF troops ___E:killed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killing_of_Yahya_Sinwar)___ Sinwar during a routine patrol and a chance encounter in southern Rafah.

In January 2025, the Wall Street Journal , citing Israeli sources, reported that Sinwar's younger brother, ___E:Mohammed Sinwar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Sinwar)___ (aka Shadow ), was leading Hamas.
Its sources said that Israel were "working hard to find him" and that he (aka Shadow ) along with Izz al-Din Haddad, of al-Qassam Brigades, were the two most senior commanders in the Gaza Strip.
On 19 January 2025, ___E:a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_2025_Gaza_war_ceasefire)___ went into effect.

In January 2025, Hamas confirmed that its senior military chief, ___E:Mohammed Deif U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Deif)___ , was killed by Israel's military in July 2024.  On 18 March 2025, Israel broke the ceasefire and shelling of the territory continued.

In March 2025, Ismail Barhoum, a member of Hamas’s political bureau was killed in an Israeli attack on ___E:Nasser Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasser_Hospital)___ in ___E:Khan Younis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khan_Yunis)___ .

In April 2025, according to the IDF, Yahya Fathi Abd al-Qader Abu Shaar, the head of Hamas' weapons smuggling network, was killed by the Israeli army.  In May 2025, there were unconfirmed reports that ___E:Mohammed Sinwar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Sinwar)___ , Hamas leader in Gaza and the brother of Yahya Sinwar, and ___E:Muhammad Shabana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Shabana)___ , commander of the Rafah Brigade, were killed by Israeli airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip.
In June 2025, the Israeli military confirmed that it had identified the body of Mohammed Sinwar through ___E:DNA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA)___ checks.

In August 2025, ___E:Abu Obaida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Obaida)___ , the spokesman for Hamas's armed wing, was killed in an Israeli aerial ___E:attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Abu_Obaida)___ .
Hamas' policy towards Israel has evolved.

Historically, Hamas envisioned a Palestinian state on all of ___E:the territory that belonged to the British Mandate for Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ (that is, from the ___E:Jordan River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_River)___ to the ___E:Mediterranean Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Sea)___ ),  and in its ___E:1988 Charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Hamas_charter)___ framed the Mandate Palestine as ‘Islamic ___E:waqf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqf)___ ’ or endowment, under sovereignty of ___E:God U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_in_Islam)___ .  : 837, 839 With Hamas's 1993 Introductory Memorandum, Hamas broke away from the uncompromising character of their religious frame, and proposed two stages of liberation of Palestine: a short-term objective to establish a Palestinian state in Gaza and the West Bank, and a long-term objective still striving to liberate Mandate Palestine in its entirety.  : 837, 839 This distinction between "short-term policy" and "long-term solution" is present in many subsequent documents.

The aim of this double policy is to create an authority on a portion of the former ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ , which would eventually lead to the restoration of Islamic sovereignty across all of ___E:(Mandatory) Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ .

In 2006, Hamas signed the ___E:Palestinian Prisoners' Document U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Prisoners%27_Document)___ which supports the quest for a Palestinian state   "on all territories occupied in 1967".

This document also recognized authority of the ___E:President of the Palestinian National Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Palestinian_National_Authority)___ to negotiate with Israel.

Hamas also signed the ___E:Cairo Declaration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Cairo_Declaration)___ in 2005, which emphasized the goal of ending ___E:the Israeli occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupied_Palestinian_territories)___ and establishing a Palestinian state on the 1967 borders.

On 2 May 2017, ___E:Khaled Mashal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khaled_Mashal)___ , chief of the ___E:Hamas Political Bureau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org#Political_Bureau)___ , presented a ___E:new Charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Hamas_charter)___ , in which Hamas accepted the establishment of a Palestinian state "on the basis of ___E:June 4, 1967 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ " ( ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ , ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ and ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ ).
But the new Charter did not recognize Israel nor relinquish Palestinian claims to all of historical Palestine.
Many scholars saw Hamas' acceptance of the 1967 borders as a tacit acceptance of another entity on the other side.

The founder of Hamas, sheikh ___E:Ahmed Yassin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Yassin)___ , has offered Israel a ten-year hudna ( ___E:armistice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice)___ ) in return for complete Israeli withdrawal from the territories captured in the 1967 war and establishing a Palestinian state in West Bank and Gaza. Later, Yassin has stated that this hudna could be renewed for 30, 40 or even 100 years.  : 238  Hamas's spokesperson, ___E:Ahmed Yousef U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Yousef)___ , has said that a "hudna" is more than a ceasefire and it "obliges parties to use the period to seek a permanent, non-violent resolution to their differences."  Under ___E:Islamic international law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharia)___ , a hudna is a binding and the ___E:Qur'an U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qur%27an)___ prohibits its violation.

Hamas first proposed a hudna in 1999. In exchange Israel would have to end the occupation of West Bank and Gaza Strip and release all ___E:Palestinian prisoners U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_prisoners)___ .

The 1999 proposal did not mention the issues of the return of the Palestinian refugees or Hamas's recognition of Israel, but interviewed Hamas leaders in 2010 added that the ___E:right of return U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_right_of_return)___ should be accepted in principle by Israel (without direct actual implementation).
Israel and Hamas should use the period of calm (armistice) for negotiating these two issues; if they would also be settled the temporary peace would convert into a permanent peace agreement.

In 2006, Ismail Haniyeh, shortly after being ___E:elected U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Palestinian_legislative_election)___ as ___E:Prime Minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_Palestinian_National_Authority)___ , sent messages both to US President ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ and to Israel's leaders, offering a long-term truce.
Neither Israel nor the United States responded.
Haniyeh's proposal reportedly was a fifty-year armistice with Israel, if a Palestinian state is created along the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital.

A Hamas official added that the armistice would renew automatically each time.  In mid-2006, ___E:University of Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maryland)___ 's Jerome Segal suggested that a Palestinian state within the 1967 borders and a truce for many years could be considered Hamas's de facto recognition of Israel.
A similar proposal was once again offered by Hamas to Israel in November 2006.

In November 2008, in a meeting, on Gaza Strip soil, with 11 ___E:European U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe)___ members of parliaments, Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh re-stated that Hamas was willing to accept a Palestinian state "in ___E:the territories of 1967 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War)___ " ( ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ and ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ ), and offered Israel a long-term truce if Israel recognized the ___E:Palestinians' national rights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_right_of_return)___ ; and stated that Israel rejected this proposal.
A Hamas finance minister around 2018 contended that such a "long-term ceasefire as understood by Hamas and a two-state settlement are the same".

According to Leila Seurat, the movement's leaders consider that a traditional peace treaty like those in the Western tradition would be tantamount to surrender, while a truce would provide an alternative allowing them to wait for an inversion in the regional balance of power to the Palestinians' advantage.

Abusada, a political scientist at ___E:Al Azhar University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Azhar_University_%E2%80%93_Gaza)___ , wrote in 2008 that Hamas talks "of hudna [temporary ceasefire], not of peace or reconciliation with Israel.

They believe over time they will be strong enough to liberate all historic Palestine."  Some scholars have noted that alongside offering a long-term truce, Hamas retains its objective of establishing one state in former ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ .  : 837, 839 Hamas originally proposed a 10-year truce, or hudna , to Israel, contingent on the creation of a Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders.
Sheikh Ahmed Yassin indicated that such truce could be extended for 30, 40, or even 100 years, but it would never signal a recognition of Israel.

A Hamas official said that having an indefinite truce with Israel doesn't contradict Hamas's lack of recognition of Israel, comparing it to the ___E:Irish Republican Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Republican_Army)___ 's willingness to accept a permanent armistice with the ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ without recognizing the UK's sovereignty over Northern Ireland.  : 221–246
Hamas leaders have repeatedly emphasized they do not recognize Israel.
But Hamas has also repeatedly accepted the 1967 borders in signed agreements (in 2005,  2006,  and 2007  ) and in its 2017 charter.

Some scholars saw Hamas' acceptance of the 1967 borders as a tacit acceptance of another entity on the other side,    while others state that Hamas retains the long-term objective of establishing one state in former Mandatory Palestine.  : 837, 839     Whether Hamas would recognize Israel in a future peace agreement is debated.
Others argue that the long-term objective and lack of official recognition of Israel is merely maintained as a bargaining chip for future negotiations.
Several scholars have compared Hamas's lack of recognition of Israel to ___E:Likud's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Likud)___ lack of recognition of a Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza.
In 1995 Hamas repeated its rejection of any recognition of Israel.

However, after Hamas won the 2006 elections, it did not implement the 1988 Charter as policy, and instead agreed to work with the existing Palestinian political system.  : 839 In the ___E:2007 Mecca agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Mecca_agreement)___ , Hamas agreed to respect previous agreements between Fatah and Israel, including the Oslo Accords in which the PLO recognized Israel.

Both in the 2007 agreement and in the 2006 ___E:Palestinian Prisoners' Document U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_Prisoners%27_Document)___ , Hamas agreed to a Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders.
Scholars see this as "implicit" recognition of Israel because by accepting a Palestinian state limited to the 1967 borders, Hamas acknowledged the existence of an entity on the other side.

Mousa Abu Marzook, then the vice-president of Hamas' Political Bureau, explained his party's position in 2011: while Hamas did not recognize Israel as a state, it considered the existence of Israel as "amr waqi" (or fait accompli, meaning something that has happened and cannot be changed).
He called this "de facto recognition" of Israel.

Likewise, ___E:Graham Usher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Usher_(journalist))___ writes that while Hamas does not consider Israel to be legitimate, it has accepted Israel as political reality.
In 2017, Hamas once again accepted the 1967 borders in its new charter that "drop[ped] the call for the destruction of Israel from its manifesto".
While it did not abrogate the old charter, Hamas leaders explained that "The original charter has now become a historical document and part of an earlier stage in our evolution.
It will remain in the movement's bookshelf as a record of our past."  Khaled Mashal stated that the new document reflected "our position for now."

Tareq Baconi, a former analyst at the ___E:International Crisis Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Crisis_Group)___ currently at ___E:Al-Shabaka U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Shabaka,_The_Palestinian_Policy_Network)___ think-tank, notes that Hamas has said it would accept mutual recognition of Israel in any consensus peace deal approved by other Palestinian parties and the population in a referendum.

To explain why it withholds formal recognition, Baconi argues that Hamas has learned from the fact that, in the 1993 Oslo Accords, the PLO made a "historic concession" in recognizing Israel on 78% of the land of historic Palestine (along the 1967 borders), but was unable to convince Israel to recognize Palestine on the remaining 22% of the land. Having already recognized Israel, the PLO was unable to use recognition to extract any further concessions from Israel, thus according to Baconi the lesson for Hamas was that you can't negotiate from a position of weakness, and the issue of formal recognition of Israel is kept as bargaining chip for negotiations.

Hamas developed its social welfare programme by replicating the model established by Egypt's Muslim Brotherhood.
For Hamas, charity and the development of one's community are both prescribed by religion and to be understood as forms of resistance.

In Islamic tradition, dawah ( lit. transl. "the call to God" ) obliges the faithful to reach out to others by both proselytising and by charitable works, and typically the latter center on the mosques which make use of both waqf endowment resources and charitable donations ( zakat , one of the five pillars of Islam) to fund grassroots services such as nurseries, schools, orphanages, soup kitchens, women's activities, library services and even sporting clubs within a larger context of preaching and political discussions.
In the 1990s, some 85% of its budget was allocated to the provision of social services.
Hamas has been called perhaps the most significant social services actor in Palestine.

By 2000, Hamas or its affiliated charities ran roughly 40% of the social institutions in the West Bank and Gaza and, with other Islamic charities, by 2005, was supporting 120,000 individuals with monthly financial support in Gaza.  Part of the appeal of these institutions is that they fill a vacuum in the administration by the PLO of the Palestinian territories, which had failed to cater to the demand for jobs and broad social services, and is widely viewed as corrupt.

As late as 2005, the budget of Hamas, drawing on global charity contributions, was mostly tied up in covering running expenses for its social programmes, which extended from the supply of housing, food and water for the needy to more general functions such as financial aid, medical assistance, educational development and religious instruction.
A certain accounting flexibility allowed these funds to cover both charitable causes and military operations, permitting transfer from one to the other.

The dawah infrastructure itself was understood, within the Palestinian context, as providing the soil from which a militant opposition to the occupation would flower. [f] In this regard it differs from the rival ___E:Palestinian Islamic Jihad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Jihad_Movement_in_Palestine)___ which lacks any social welfare network, and relies on spectacular terrorist attacks to recruit adherents.

In 2007, through funding from Iran, Hamas managed to allocate at a cost of $60 million, monthly stipends of $100 for 100,000 workers, and a similar sum for 3,000 fishermen ___E:laid idle by Israel's imposition of restrictions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip#Effect_on_the_fishing_industry)___ on fishing offshore, plus grants totalling $45 million to detainees and their families.  ___E:Matthew Levitt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Levitt)___ argues that Hamas grants to people are subject to a rigorous cost-benefit analysis of how beneficiaries will support Hamas, with those linked to terrorist activities receiving more than others.

Israel holds the families of suicide bombers accountable and bulldozes their homes, whereas the families of Hamas activists who have been killed or wounded during militant operations are given an initial, one-time grant varying between $500–$5,000, together with a $100 monthly allowance.
Rent assistance is also given to families whose homes have been destroyed by Israeli bombing though families unaffiliated with Hamas are said to receive less.
Until 2007, these activities extended to the West Bank, but, after a PLO crackdown, now continue exclusively in the Gaza Strip.

The group's ideology outlines its aim as the liberation of Palestine and the restoration of Palestinian rights under the dispensations set forth in the Qur'an, and this translates into three policy priorities:

To evoke the spirit of Jihad (Resistance) among Palestinians, Arabs, and Muslims; to defend Palestinians and their land against the Zionist occupation and its manifestations; to liberate Palestinians and their land that was usurped by the Zionist occupation forces and settlers.
